svg.text: DigitLab v0.2 / finite attack survival is not all-domain correctness
Exact box margins for the already selected linear model. No retraining. Nonlinear MLP remains uncertified.
1 Exact real arithmetic, with a narrow and explicit scope
Every loaded binary64 coefficient becomes an exact rational. Shared coefficient denominator:
Inputs: exact original counts / 16. Epsilon: the displayed rational, not its binary approximation.
This certifies the real affine function, not every floating-point execution. Clean and all 7,188 witness predictions agree with NumPy.
2 Correct on every point in [0,1] intersect the L-infinity box
. The exact result includes all competitors, pixel clipping and lowest-class-index ties.
PGD survivors with an attained failure: radius 1/10 =
3 Why clipping and ties cannot be dropped
Clipping control: z0 = 20x + 1, z1 = 0; x = 1/10, radius 1/5.
Valid box [0, 3/10]: minimum true-class margin = 1. Ignoring pixel bounds gives -1, at invalid x = -1/10.
Tie control: z0 = x, z1 = 0; x = 1/2, radius 1/2. Minimum margin = 0, yet label 0 is always correct.
Switch to z1 = x, z0 = 0 and label 1: the same zero minimum fails at x = 0. Lowest class index wins.
4 Actual PGD survivors with exact attaining failures at radius 1/10

These are first three PGD survivors with exact failures, not a representative image sample.
All 64,692 competitor minima and 7,188 attaining witness decisions are retained in the four radius reports.
The proof is coordinatewise: minimize each margin term at its valid lower/upper endpoint according to its sign.
Data/images: Alpaydin & Kaynak (1998), UCI DOI 10.24432/C50P49, CC BY 4.0. Witness images are adaptations.
Established affine-box optimization, not a new algorithm, MLP certificate, perceptual guarantee or production OCR claim.
